known_facts_book1: The good Sorceress of Oz, whose palace is in the Quadling Country, attended by a hundred of the most beautiful girls in Oz as maids of honor; Ozma is the only one in all the land Glinda bows to.

Owns the **Great Book of Records**, in which a record of every event anywhere in the world is printed at the moment it happens; it is chained to a marble table with golden chains and locked with **five jeweled padlocks** whose keys she carries in her bosom.
Had never heard of the Flatheads or the Skeezers before this book, and admits her sorcery can learn little about either, because both are magic-workers.
Advises Ozma, honestly and unsuccessfully, that she might simply pay no attention to a quarrel she would never have known about.
Gives Dorothy the **alarm ring** — one turn right, one turn left rings a bell in Glinda's palace — with strict instructions to use it only in danger of destruction.
**Fails, repeatedly and openly**: she can find no magic to raise a sunken island, builds a model island in a pond by her castle to experiment on, and every experiment fails.
Travels to the Emerald City by stork chariot, then sends the chariot home so the whole Rescue Expedition can keep together on foot.
Saves Button Bright from a tiger and a wolf by fixing both beasts to the ground with an incantation, having first found him in a small round mirror dusted with white powder.
Makes the abandoned submarine obey **sorcery** instead of witchcraft, using magic recipe No. 1163, the Wizard's skeropythrope, a powder and a vial of liquid.
Is stopped by the marble basement door, which was commanded to open only to one magic word — no other magic word can move it, and Coo-ee-oh has forgotten it.
Recognises the grayish powder in the hidden drawer as **Gaulau**, a rare mineral powder known to sorcerers, more wonderful than radium.
Takes Scraps's joke seriously — draw down the lake — and turns it into the plan that works: lower the water until the Dome shows, and remove one pane.
Refills the lake afterward with an incantation recited from the bridge with the Wizard and the Adepts.
**Ends the Flathead problem by opening every can of brains**, spreading the contents on each flat head and growing the head over them — so no one can ever be robbed of brains again.

known_relations_book1.Ozma: Her Ruler and friend, whom she rescues.
known_relations_book1.Dorothy: Whom she arms with the alarm ring.
known_relations_book1.the Wizard of Oz: Her pupil and co-leader of the expedition.
known_relations_book1.the three Adepts: The magic-workers who join her and supply the missing knowledge.
known_relations_book1.Coo-ee-oh: The witch whose stolen arts she has to reconstruct.

not_in_this_book: Glinda raises the island by her own sorcery

known_facts_book1: A little bald man with a shiny head, a merry twinkle in his eyes and the spryness of a schoolboy, second only to Glinda in all the mystic arts, having been taught by her.
Is, with Glinda, one of only two people permitted by law to practice wizardry or sorcery in Oz, and both use it only for good.
Is not as powerful as Glinda, Dorothy says, because Glinda did not teach him everything she knows — but what he knows he knows very well.
Argues, and is agreed with, that the expedition should go to the lake first and punish the Su-dic afterward, so nothing delays the rescue.
Carries the **skeropythrope** in his black bag and hands it to Glinda for the boat-enchantment.
Says plainly that he is helpless to raise the island himself — 'Leave that to Glinda.'
First raises the idea of finding and restoring the three enchanted fishes, which turns out to be the key, though he cannot see how to single them out of a whole lake.
Meets the three restored Adepts on the shore, guesses at once they are important, and asks them no questions because he sees they do not wish to be questioned.
Removes one large pane from the Dome with tools from his black bag and goes down the rope first, hand over hand, ahead of everyone.
Rigs a chair on the doubled rope so Glinda and the Adepts can be lowered comfortably.
Refuses to let Scraps transform the lake's fishes into polliwogs: it is wicked to transform any living creature without its consent, and the lake belongs to the fishes.

known_relations_book1.Glinda: His teacher and the leader of the expedition.
known_relations_book1.Ozma: The Ruler he goes to rescue.
known_relations_book1.the three Adepts: Whom he escorts to Glinda's tent without prying.
known_relations_book1.Ervic: The Skeezer he first sees trailing behind the three maidens.

not_in_this_book: the Wizard opens the marble door
